notes: The family accumulated native shadows, chronological implementation modules, and host/generated adapters across locally safe migrations. This is an architecture and autonomous-development pressure, not evidence that generic language capability is missing.

reproducer.actual: Multiple repositories contain a mature implementation beside a native shadow or v1/v2 implementation source; agents can choose locally safe paths that create family-wide semantic duplication.
reproducer.expected: Every internal capability has one current semantic implementation, explicit owner, and an auditable convergence path for any temporary shadow.

requiredBehavior: Commons publishes a compact architecture model that identifies canonical owner/path, distinguishes implementation evolution from wire compatibility, and validates duplicate active implementations, unjustified chronological paths, ownership collisions, and shadow convergence fields.
summary: Independent migration agents preserved behavior by layering native shadows and v1/v2 modules beside mature implementations. The family now needs machine-readable canonical ownership and retirement rules so safe local choices do not fork semantics.
title: Autonomous development accumulates duplicate capability implementations
